questions.prompt: What's the deck's view of the Skills Assessment?
options: It's an objective test
It's a self-report - its value depends entirely on your honesty
It's marked by your tutor
It doesn't matter
questions.explanation: Its value depends entirely on your honesty - inflate it and you get a useless picture of yourself.

questions.prompt: What does the deck say UCAS requires, and when?
options: UCAS runs in Year 1; the material for a personal statement is built in Year 2
UCAS runs in Year 2; the material for a personal statement is built in Year 1
UCAS runs after you leave college
UCAS is optional
questions.explanation: UCAS runs in Year 2; the material for a personal statement is built in Year 1.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: the T Levels require ____ hours of industry placement.
questions.template: The T Levels require ____ hours of industry placement.
questions.explanation: Industry placement - 315 hours on the T Levels.

options: Log at the end of year 2
One entry per activity, logged the same week, tagged to the skills it evidences - ten minutes now saves an afternoon in Year 2
Only log assessed units
Only log live media
questions.explanation: One entry per activity, logged the same week, tagged to the skills it evidences.

questions.prompt: What does the deck say about Year 1 in relation to Year 2?
options: Year 1 is a warm-up
Year 1 sets the trajectory of Year 2 - it is not a warm-up
Year 1 doesn't count
Year 1 is just induction
questions.explanation: Year 1 sets the trajectory of Year 2 - it is not a warm-up.

questions.prompt: Which of these are in the first-two-weeks checklist? Select all that apply.
options: Skills Assessment completed honestly
Next Destination set, entry requirements checked
Career Quiz completed, every profile reviewed
Digital CV Introduction written
questions.explanation: All four are in the eight-item checklist.

questions.prompt: What does the deck say about part-time work?
options: Don't bother logging it
Professionalism and communication are the same skills - log it
It doesn't help your Digital CV
Only paid work in the industry counts
questions.explanation: Part-time work - professionalism and communication are the same skills.
